answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake bond before trading. Reputation then accrues only through completed, verified work — slowly, like an island rising grain by grain — so a fresh fake has no standing. Proven fraud slashes the bond to its nadir, zero, and the identity is burned. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must fund every bond, and the ivory-tower shortcut of buying reputation fails because reputation is earned over time and can never be transferred or sold.
